evidence.claim: Modi's disclosure for 31-03-2022 reports cash in hand of Rs 35,250, bank balance of Rs 46,555, FDR/MOD of Rs 2,10,33,226, NSC of Rs 9,05,105, life insurance of Rs 1,89,305, four gold rings valued at Rs 1,73,063, gross assets of Rs 2,23,82,504, no shares or personal loans, and no immovable assets.
evidence.title: Details of the Assets: Movable and Immovable of Myself, My Spouse, and All Dependents on 31-03-2022
evidence.excerpt: Modi's disclosure for 31-03-2022 reports cash in hand of Rs 35,250, bank balance of Rs 46,555, FDR/MOD of Rs 2,10,33,226, NSC of Rs 9,05,105, life insurance of Rs 1,89,305, four gold rings valued at Rs 1,73,063, gross assets of Rs 2,23,82,504, no shares or personal loans, and no immovable assets.
evidence.source_locator: Pages 0-3, asset tables and immovable-assets section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary PMO disclosure with exact line items and explicit asset categories.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 annual disclosure as of 31 March 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong and direct: self-disclosed by Modi through the PMO; this supports transparency but does not by itself prove broader honesty on all issues.
contrary_evidence: It is a voluntary self-declaration, so completeness still depends on truthful reporting.

evidence.claim: The 31-03-2023 disclosure again lists no immovable property for Modi and reports a gross total asset value of Rs 2,58,96,444, showing continuity in public asset reporting across years.
evidence.title: Details of the Assets and Liabilities of the Union Council of Ministers (2022-2023) as on 31.03.2023
evidence.excerpt: The 31-03-2023 disclosure again lists no immovable property for Modi and reports a gross total asset value of Rs 2,58,96,444, showing continuity in public asset reporting across years.
evidence.source_locator: Pages 0-3, asset tables and immovable-assets section
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary PMO filing with precise line items and a direct year-over-year follow-up to the 2022 disclosure.
evidence.period_fit: Near-period continuity evidence immediately after the 2022 target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong and direct for Modi's own asset disclosure behavior; still limited to the asset dimension of integrity.
contrary_evidence: As with any self-filed disclosure, the document is not independent proof of completeness.

evidence.claim: NITI Aayog said Parameswaran Iyer became its CEO on 11 July 2022 and highlighted over 25 years of water-and-sanitation experience, including spearheading the Swachh Bharat Mission and serving as Secretary in the Drinking Water and Sanitation ministry.
evidence.title: NITI Aayog Welcomes Parameswaran Iyer as Its CEO
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: NITI Aayog said Parameswaran Iyer became its CEO on 11 July 2022 and highlighted over 25 years of water-and-sanitation experience, including spearheading the Swachh Bharat Mission and serving as Secretary in the Drinking Water and Sanitation ministry.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary appointment release with a detailed professional background and exact date.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong: PMO-linked senior administrative appointment; positive for professional staffing, though not proof that every appointment was merit-only.
contrary_evidence: The appointment does not alone demonstrate broader anti-nepotism practice across government.

evidence.claim: The NITI Aayog circulars page publicly lists the July 2022 appointment notification for Shri Parameswaran Iyer as CEO and the December 2022 appointment notification for Shri Arvind Virmani as Member.
evidence.title: NITI Aayog (notifications index)
evidence.publication_date: 2022-12-01 (best available for the listed notification entry)
evidence.excerpt: The NITI Aayog circulars page publicly lists the July 2022 appointment notification for Shri Parameswaran Iyer as CEO and the December 2022 appointment notification for Shri Arvind Virmani as Member.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official public index of notifications, directly linking the relevant 2022 appointment entries.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong at the level of transparency around appointments; limited because the index does not explain appointment criteria or independence.
contrary_evidence: A public notification list is not evidence that all appointments were merit-based.

evidence.claim: The article says Gautam Adani is seen by independent observers as a close aide to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and that the Adani Group has received massive government contracts in energy and infrastructure; it also describes lawsuits and other pressure faced by journalists investigating the group.
evidence.title: Adani Watch piece on Adani coverage and pressure
evidence.publisher: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism
evidence.excerpt: The article says Gautam Adani is seen by independent observers as a close aide to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and that the Adani Group has received massive government contracts in energy and infrastructure; it also describes lawsuits and other pressure faced by journalists investigating the group.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reputable research-journalism outlet summarizing investigative reporting and observer claims; useful but still inferential on Modi-specific favoritism.
evidence.period_fit: Explains a 2022-anchored patronage/favoritism controversy but is published just after the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate and indirect: the article links the network to Modi through observers' inference, not a direct finding of Modi personal benefit or instruction.
contrary_evidence: The piece is not a formal finding of corruption and relies partly on outside observers' interpretation.
